who: Booker T. Washington · Up from Slavery, 1901
quote: I have learned that success is to be measured not so much by the position that one has reached in life as by the obstacles which he has overcome while trying to succeed.
meaning: Born a slave, he went 500 miles to find a school. In 1881 he opened his own school.

quote: Our strength grows out of our weakness.
meaning: The weak places in you are where your strength starts to grow.

quote: Although the world is full of suffering, it is full also of the overcoming of it.
meaning: She could not see or hear. In 1904 she finished university. Hard things can be beaten.

quote: There is nothing in the world more soft and weak than water, and yet for attacking things that are firm and strong there is nothing that can take precedence of it.
meaning: Water is soft, but it wears down rock. Soft and patient wins.

who: Katsushika Hokusai · One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji, 1834
quote: ...nothing I did before the age of seventy was worthy of attention. At seventy-three, I began to grasp the structures of birds and beasts, insects and fish...
meaning: He made his famous Great Wave at about 70. It is never too late to get better.

quote: It becomes firmly grounded by long constant efforts with great love.
meaning: Practice every day, for a long time, with love. Then it stays strong.

quote: Feet, what do I need them for if I have wings to fly?
meaning: Polio as a child. A bad accident at 18. She painted from her bed and became a famous artist.

who: Mencius · Book VI, Part II, 15 (tr. Legge)
quote: ...when Heaven is about to confer a great office on any man, it first exercises his mind with suffering, and his sinews and bones with toil.
meaning: Before a big job, life gives you hard training. The hard days are the training.

who: Wilbur Wright · Letter to Octave Chanute, 1900
quote: It is possible to fly without motors, but not without knowledge and skill.
meaning: Two bicycle makers studied birds for years. In 1903 they flew the first plane.

who: Friedrich Nietzsche · Human, All Too Human, 163
quote: Do not talk of gifts, of inborn talents! We could mention great men of all kinds who were but little gifted.
meaning: Stop saying "I have no talent." Many great people had little talent. They kept working.
